source.title: Decoding Dark Matter: Specialized Sparse Autoencoders for Interpreting Rare Concepts in Foundation Models
source.authors: Aashiq Muhamed; Mona T. Diab; Virginia Smith

record.tranche_reason: The study reports how changing the SAE training objective changes reconstruction errors and discusses SAE error nodes in causal feature circuits, refining claims about the nature and training dependence of SAE error.
record.gate_note: The study's reconstruction-perplexity comparisons do not compare SAE reconstruction errors with random errors of the same size, so they do not test that part of V3. Its results about error nodes and new SSAE features are recorded below; cited findings from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The paper uses 'dark matter' in Templeton et al.'s sense: rare concepts that SAEs fail to learn as features. It does not mean the structure of the SAE error vector. It never measures how linearly predictable the error is (V1). It never compares error norms across SAE sizes (V2). It never compares spliced-in loss against random errors of matched size (V3). It never splits the error into linear and nonlinear parts (V4). It never shows how much of a circuit's or steering result's behaviour is lost when error terms are dropped (V5). It never tests whether dark matter is a training artifact (V6). Error nodes appear only qualitatively, as triangles in circuit figures (App. H). The TERM-vs-ERM reconstruction-error comparison on TinyStories concerns how a tail-focused objective redistributes error. It does not test whether error shrinks with better training. None of these results gives a rate or share for any version, so the study does not test the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors conclude that SSAEs, trained by dense-retrieval finetuning with TERM, capture rare subdomain concepts better than general SAEs and give more interpretable features. They report comparable spliced perplexity in the typical L0 range. In the Bias in Bios case study, SSAEs improve worst-group accuracy by 12.5% when used to remove spurious gender information. TERM lowers tail and maximum reconstruction error at a slight cost in average error. 'Dark matter' here means unlearned rare features, not the structure of the SAE error.
record.recipe_differences: The study specializes pretrained SAEs by subdomain retrieval and finetuning, and compares ERM with TERM; it does not reproduce the original study's proposed error-structure measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction error outcomes depend on the training objective: TERM lowers tail-token and maximum error but slightly raises average error.

fits_no_version.finding: Finetuning GSAEs on retrieved subdomain data (SSAE) adds features that, per the authors, explain variance previously attributed to GSAE error nodes in the Bias in Bios circuit. No magnitude is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Part of SAE error in a narrow domain consists of domain-specific features that targeted finetuning can recover.

fits_no_version.finding: A tilted (minimax) objective lowers maximum and tail-token reconstruction error but slightly raises average error on a TinyStories-1M SAE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The training objective redistributes SAE error across frequent and rare tokens without reducing total error.

record.code_released: The authors state that code, experiments, and ablations will be publicly released upon acceptance; no URL is stated.
record.peer_reviewed: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: No random-error-matched comparison is reported. The error-structure claims are not tested across SAE sizes. The TinyStories reconstruction-error descriptions provide no numeric values or uncertainty estimates. The circuit results do not directly compare behavior with error nodes retained versus omitted.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results were left out.

untested.parts: All; no linear prediction of error from activations.
All; no comparison across SAE sizes of error norms or failure contexts.
All; spliced perplexity is reported but never compared with random errors of matched norm.
All; no linear/nonlinear split of the error. The finding that SSAE features absorb error-node variance is unquantified.
Share of circuit or steering behaviour lost without error terms; error nodes are shown only qualitatively.
All; no test of sparsity penalty, shrinkage, dead latents, architecture or end-to-end training as the source of error.

missing.what: Indirect-effect magnitudes of error nodes, compared with feature nodes, in the GSAE and SSAE circuits. These would be needed to read V5.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's labels used label names in the version field and were invalid. The study shares the 'dark matter' term with the original source but addresses a different question: coverage of rare features. The error-term observations are qualitative and do not support verdicts on any version.

versions.untested_parts: No test of whether SAE error vectors are linearly predictable from input activations.
No comparison across SAE sizes of per-token error norms, failure contexts, or whether error vanishes with scale.
The study reports perplexity with SAE reconstructions, but does not compare the resulting loss harm with random errors of the same size.
No separation of linear and nonlinear error, nor test of whether either part corresponds to unlearned features or resists further dictionary learning.

The study reports causal relevance of SAE error nodes and features that explain variance attributed to error nodes, but does not compare model behavior with the error term retained versus omitted, or test steering.

The study changes the training objective and measures reconstruction-error outcomes, but does not establish that dark matter mostly arises from training artifacts, test alternative architectures or end-to-end training, or compare the magnitude of training effects with representation structure.

rows.subject: TinyStories-1M
rows.operation_detail: Compared GSAEs trained with ERM and TERM (tilt=10^9) on the 7th-layer residual stream.
rows.measure: Reconstruction error and error variance by token frequency rank
rows.value: TERM reduces reconstruction error and error variance for tail tokens compared to ERM.
rows.note: The text describes the direction of the tail-token result; no numeric values are given.
rows.check: TERM vs ERM per-token-rank reconstruction error on a width-64 SAE measures how a different objective redistributes error across frequent and rare tokens. It does not test whether dark matter mostly reflects training choices or shrinks with better training. The result is figure-only, with no numbers. It should not be linked to V6.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.2.1, experimental setup and results; Figure 3 caption.

rows.subject: TinyStories-1M
rows.operation_detail: Compared the reconstruction-error distributions of TERM-trained and ERM-trained GSAEs.
rows.value: TERM-trained GSAE minimizes maximum error at the cost of slightly higher average error.
rows.note: The reported tradeoff shows that the objective affects error, but does not establish that most SAE error is a training artifact.
rows.check: TERM lowers maximum error but slightly raises average error, so total error does not shrink. This is a tradeoff between objectives, not a test of V6. The result is figure-only (Fig. 22) and the text gives no values.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.2.1 results; Appendix N.4; Figure 22 caption.

rows.subject: Pythia-70M
rows.operation_detail: Computed indirect effects for feature and SAE-error nodes in a sparse feature circuit for the Bias in Bios classifier.
rows.measure: Causal relevance of SAE error nodes in the feature circuit
rows.value: The circuit includes causally relevant error terms not captured by the SAE.
rows.note: The paper describes error terms as circuit nodes and reports that they are causally relevant; it does not quantify the effect of omitting them.
rows.check: Error nodes appear as causally relevant triangles in the circuit figure (Fig. 15). The text gives no indirect-effect values and no share of behaviour lost when they are omitted. The magnitude V5 requires cannot be read.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix H, circuit construction and description of triangular error nodes; Figure 15 caption.

rows.subject: Pythia-70M
rows.operation_detail: Compared activated feature counts for a finetuned SSAE and GSAE and examined the resulting classifier circuit.
rows.measure: Activated feature count and variance previously attributed to GSAE error nodes
rows.value: SSAE: 908 activated features; the additional features play a role in the sparse feature circuits and explain more variance previously attributed to GSAE error nodes.
rows.note: This supports functional relevance of SAE error terms, but does not test whether keeping the error term is necessary for preserving behavior.
rows.check: The 908 vs 602 figure counts activated features, not error. The claim that new features explain variance once attributed to error nodes is stated without numbers. The row compares the study's own method (SSAE) with the GSAE, not a measure of error carrying function. 'Partial' is unsupported.

relation.reason: The paper discusses missing rare features and SAE error nodes without testing the catalog's specific claims or relying on those claims as established findings.

tranche.reason: Rare-concept coverage and objective-dependent error redistribution do not measure V1–V6. Causally relevant error nodes are identified, but behavior lost upon omitting them is not measured.

source_check.notes: R2's qualitative tradeoff is explicitly stated in Sections 3.2.1 and N.4, rather than being figure-only. R3 does not establish V5's meaningful behavioral loss; its version link should be none.
